responsibility: `rustc_typeck` implements Rust’s semantic type-checking pipeline for a crate, turning HIR item and body syntax into the compiler’s internal type information, validating that those types and impls are legal, and emitting the diagnostics and lints associated with type checking. Its `lib.rs` root wires the crate’s query providers and major phases together: collection of item-level type facts, outlives and variance computation, impl well-formedness checking, coherence, item/body type checking, unused-item linting, and entry-point validation, while also exposing helper conversions from HIR forms into internal type and predicate representations. The collect phase is split between the root `collect.rs`, which walks item-like definitions to compute item signatures, generics, predicates, trait/impl metadata, codegen attributes, and related body-independent semantic facts, and the `collect` module, whose `type_of` and `item_bounds` logic derives canonical item `Ty` values and elaborated predicate bounds, including handling opaque or underspecified types and implicit `Sized` requirements. The `astconv` module provides the AST/HIR-to-`ty` conversion layer used throughout these phases, lowering type syntax, paths, trait objects, associated items, bounds, lifetimes, and generic arguments into `rustc_middle::ty` forms; its `generics` support validates generic argument use, and its internal `errors` logic diagnoses conversion-specific failures. The root `bounds.rs` complements this by holding the in-memory representation of converted type, lifetime, and projection bounds and flattening them into canonical predicate lists consumed by later queries and checks. For semantic checking of executable code and item bodies, the `check` module performs item and body type checking: it builds checking contexts, validates signatures and intrinsics, pre-gathers locals, checks expressions, patterns, operators, method calls, casts, closures, generators, matches, and trait/impl relationships, applies inference, coercions, autoderef, divergence and region reasoning, analyzes upvar capture and generator interiors, and writes final per-body type results. Supporting HIR-level analyses for this body checking include `mem_categorization.rs`, which normalizes expressions and patterns into typed memory places with projections, dereferences, mutability, and upvar information, and `expr_use_visitor.rs`, which walks bodies to classify uses such as moves, copies, borrows, mutations, bindings, and fake reads so downstream borrow-check-related analyses can reason about value usage. The crate also computes foundational type-system metadata used by later compiler stages: `outlives` derives explicit and inferred lifetime outlives requirements for items, including structural inference for ADTs and implied bounds queries; `variance` runs crate-wide variance inference for generic parameters and exposes the results through queries and test hooks. Impl legality is enforced in two layers: the root `constrained_generic_params.rs` computes which impl generics are actually constrained, and the root `impl_wf_check.rs` performs early impl well-formedness checks such as rejecting unconstrained generics, duplicate impl items, and invalid specialization setup, while the `impl_wf_check` module specifically enforces `min_specialization`’s refinement and always-applicable rules. At the crate level, `coherence` then checks that impls are globally legal and non-overlapping, enforcing orphan and overlap rules, validating unsafety, polarity, and `may_dangle`, applying the extra rules for built-in traits like `Drop`, `Copy`, `CoerceUnsized`, and `DispatchFromDyn`, and collecting valid inherent impls for later lookup. Diagnostic infrastructure is shared across the crate through the root `errors.rs`, which defines reusable typed diagnostic payloads for typeck and collection errors, the `structured_errors` module, which centralizes richer context-sensitive builders for selected type-system mistakes, and the root `structured_errors.rs`, which defines the common `StructuredDiagnostic` abstraction and reexports those builders; `hir_wf_check.rs` further improves well-formedness diagnostics by rechecking nested HIR types to pinpoint better spans and causes. Finally, `check_unused.rs` performs post-typeck lints for unused imports and extern crates based on what trait imports body checking actually required. Together, these modules make `rustc_typeck` the compiler component responsible for collecting type information, converting Rust syntax into internal type representations, validating item, impl, and body type correctness, computing supporting variance and lifetime facts, and producing the primary diagnostics and lints associated with Rust type checking.
